segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ לֹא יִשְׂכּוֹר אָדָם פּוֹעֲלִים בְּשַׁבָּת. וְלֹא יֹאמַר אָדָם לַחֲבֵירוֹ לִשְׂכּוֹר לוֹ פּוֹעֲלִים. אֵין מַחְשִׁיכִין עַל הַתְּחוּם לִשְׂכּוֹר לוֹ פּוֹעֲלִים וּלְהָבִיא פֵּירוֹת, אֲבָל מַחְשִׁיךְ הוּא לִשְׁמוֹר, וּמֵבִיא פֵּירוֹת בְּיָדוֹ. כְּלָל אָמַר אַבָּא שָׁאוּל: כׇּל שֶׁאֲנִי זַכַּאי בַּאֲמִירָתוֹ — רַשַּׁאי אֲנִי לְהַחְשִׁיךְ עָלָיו.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» «A person may not hire workers on Shabbat» to work for him after Shabbat because even speaking about weekday matters is prohibited on Shabbat. Similarly, «a person may not tell another» on Shabbat «to hire workers for him. One may not» even «wait for nightfall at» the edge of «the Shabbat boundary» in order to leave the boundary immediately after Shabbat «to hire workers for himself or to bring produce» from his field. «But he may wait for nightfall» at the edge of the Shabbat boundary in order «to guard» his produce that is outside the Shabbat boundary, «and» he may then «bring produce» back «in his hand,» since he did not initially intend to wait at the edge of the boundary for this purpose. «Abba Shaul stated a» general «principle:» With regard to «anything that I am permitted to discuss» on Shabbat, «I am permitted to wait for nightfall» at the edge of the Shabbat boundary «for its sake.»
